# aikido_container (Resource)

Manages activation and configuration of an existing Aikido container. The container must already exist in Aikido (discovered from a registry or a cloud); this resource never creates or deletes it. Apply sets active and optional config; destroy deactivates it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Activate and configure an existing Aikido container.
resource "aikido_container" "example" {
  id     = "12345"
  active = true

  # Supports * wildcards and the special value semver-production.
  tag_filter = "prod-*"

  sensitivity  = "sensitive"
  connectivity = "connected"

  labels = ["production"]

  # Written only when set. Removing it leaves the existing link in place.
  linked_code_repo_id = 67
}

# Omitting tag_filter leaves the container's filter alone.
resource "aikido_container" "development" {
  id     = "12346"
  active = true
}

# The empty string scans the newest image.
resource "aikido_container" "staging" {
  id         = "12347"
  active     = true
  tag_filter = ""
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the container is activated for scanning in Aikido. Public images and self-managed SBOM uploads cannot be deactivated: Aikido rejects the request and they have to be deleted instead.
- `id` (String) Aikido container ID. Import accepts the numeric ID or registry_name/name (optionally @tag_filter). registry_name is whatever Aikido reports for that registry (for example an AWS account ID, GCP project ID, ACR hostname, or Docker Hub namespace).

### Optional

- `connectivity` (String) Whether the container runs on an internet-connected server. One of: connected, not_connected, unknown.
- `labels` (Set of String) Label names managed by this resource. When set, Terraform creates/deletes labels to match. Omitting labels leaves Aikido labels untouched. An empty set deletes every user-created label currently on the container. Labels imported from external sources are reported by data sources but cannot be managed here: they are left unchanged, and naming one is rejected.
- `linked_code_repo_id` (Number) Aikido code repository ID to link to this container. Written only when set; removing it from the configuration leaves the existing link in place rather than unlinking.
- `sensitivity` (String) Sensitivity level of the container. One of: extreme, sensitive, normal, not_sensitive, no_data.
- `tag_filter` (String) Tag filter deciding which image is scanned. Supports * wildcards, for example prod-*, and the special value semver-production. Omitting it leaves the container's current filter alone; set it to the empty string to scan the newest image instead. Aikido rejects a tag filter on public images and on self-managed SBOM uploads, and on a container whose clone in the same region already carries the same filter.

### Read-Only

- `cloud_id` (Number) ID of the cloud acting as the registry for this container. Null when the container came from a registry.
- `distro` (String) Linux distribution detected in the scanned image.
- `distro_version` (String) Version of the detected distribution.
- `last_scanned_at` (Number) Unix timestamp of the last completed scan.
- `last_scanned_digest` (String) Digest of the scanned image.
- `last_scanned_tag` (String) Tag that was actually scanned, as opposed to the tag_filter that selected it.
- `name` (String) Name of the container.
- `registry_id` (Number) ID of the registry holding this container. Null when the container was discovered through a cloud.
- `registry_name` (String) Name of the registry holding this container. Provider-specific: for example an AWS account ID, GCP project ID, ACR hostname, or Docker Hub namespace.
- `registry_provider` (String) Provider hosting the container (e.g. aws, acr, docker-hub).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Containers can be imported by their numeric Aikido container ID.
terraform import aikido_container.example 12345

# Or by registry_name/name for containers discovered from a registry.
# Use the registry_name and name returned by the Aikido API (or aikido_containers).
#
# Examples of registry_name by provider:
#   AWS ECR:       12-digit account ID
#   GCP Artifact:  project ID
#   Azure ACR:     registry hostname (e.g. myregistry.azurecr.io)
#   Docker Hub:    namespace or organization
#   Self-hosted:   registry hostname
terraform import aikido_container.example 111222333444/pied-piper/compression
terraform import aikido_container.example myregistry.azurecr.io/event-bus
terraform import aikido_container.example acme-corp/api-gateway

# Append @tag_filter when several clones share the same registry and name.
terraform import aikido_container.example '111222333444/pied-piper/compression@prod-*'

# A trailing @ selects the container that scans its newest image.
terraform import aikido_container.example '111222333444/pied-piper/compression@'
```
